# Resource: stripe_subscription

A customer's recurring purchase of one or more prices. `terraform destroy` cancels the subscription immediately, because Stripe cannot delete one: billing stops and the cancelled subscription stays in the account. `items` are matched by `price`: an item whose price stays keeps its ID and changes in place, a new price adds an item, a dropped price deletes it, and a reorder changes nothing. A price may appear once. An item added from outside, such as one that `stripe_subscription_item` created, is not part of `items` and is never changed or deleted by this resource. An update that changes `items` also takes `proration_behavior` and `payment_behavior`. An item that sets `price_data` has no price of its own to match by, so it is matched by its `price_data`: changing its quantity, metadata or other settings updates the item in place, and changing its `price_data` replaces the item, which gets a new item ID. Two items may not carry identical `price_data`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_customer" "acme" {
  email = "billing@acme.example"
}

resource "stripe_product" "plan" {
  name = "Team plan"
}

resource "stripe_price" "monthly" {
  product     = stripe_product.plan.id
  currency    = "usd"
  unit_amount = 2000

  recurring = {
    interval = "month"
  }
}

# Invoiced by email, so the customer needs no payment method.
resource "stripe_subscription" "team" {
  customer          = stripe_customer.acme.id
  collection_method = "send_invoice"
  days_until_due    = 30

  items = [{
    price    = stripe_price.monthly.id
    quantity = 5
  }]
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are optional:

* `add_invoice_items` - (Optional) A list of prices and quantities that will generate invoice items appended to the next invoice for this subscription. You may pass up to 20 items. See [`add_invoice_items`](#add_invoice_items) below.
* `application_fee_percent` - (Optional) A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The request must be made by a platform account on a connected account in order to set an application fee percentage. For more information, see the application fees [documentation](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/subscriptions#collecting-fees-on-subscriptions).
* `automatic_tax` - (Optional) Automatic tax settings for this subscription. See [`automatic_tax`](#automatic_tax) below.
* `backdate_start_date` - (Optional) A past timestamp to backdate the subscription's start date to. If set, the first invoice will contain line items for the timespan between the start date and the current time. Can be combined with trials and the billing cycle anchor. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `billing_cycle_anchor` - (Optional) A future timestamp in UTC format to anchor the subscription's [billing cycle](https://docs.stripe.com/subscriptions/billing-cycle). The anchor is the reference point that aligns future billing cycle dates. It sets the day of week for `week` intervals, the day of month for `month` and `year` intervals, and the month of year for `year` intervals. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `billing_cycle_anchor_config` - (Optional) Mutually exclusive with billing_cycle_anchor and only valid with monthly and yearly price intervals. When provided, the billing_cycle_anchor is set to the next occurrence of the day_of_month at the hour, minute, and second UTC. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`billing_cycle_anchor_config`](#billing_cycle_anchor_config) below.
* `billing_mode` - (Optional) Controls how prorations and invoices for subscriptions are calculated and orchestrated. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`billing_mode`](#billing_mode) below.
* `billing_schedules` - (Optional) An array of billing schedules, which allow you to bill customers in advance for multiple service periods. Requires flexible billing mode and API version 2026-05-27.dahlia or later. Learn more about [prebilling](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/prebilling). See [`billing_schedules`](#billing_schedules) below.
* `billing_thresholds` - (Optional) Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the subscription advanced to a new billing period. When updating, pass an empty string to remove previously-defined thresholds. See [`billing_thresholds`](#billing_thresholds) below.
* `cancel_at` - (Optional) A timestamp at which the subscription should cancel. If set to a date before the current period ends, this will cause a proration if prorations have been enabled using `proration_behavior`. If set during a future period, this will always cause a proration for that period.
* `cancel_at_period_end` - (Optional) Indicate whether this subscription should cancel at the end of the current period (`current_period_end`). Defaults to `false`.
* `cancellation_details` - (Optional) Details about why this subscription was cancelled See [`cancellation_details`](#cancellation_details) below.
* `collection_method` - (Optional) Either `charge_automatically`, or `send_invoice`. When charging automatically, Stripe will attempt to pay this subscription at the end of the cycle using the default source attached to the customer. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as `active`. Defaults to `charge_automatically`. Possible values: `charge_automatically`, `send_invoice`.
* `currency` - (Optional) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Changing it replaces the resource.
* `customer` - (Optional) The identifier of the customer to subscribe. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `customer_account` - (Optional) The identifier of the account representing the customer to subscribe. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `days_until_due` - (Optional) Number of days a customer has to pay invoices generated by this subscription. Valid only for subscriptions where `collection_method` is set to `send_invoice`.
* `default_payment_method` - (Optional) ID of the default payment method for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription. This takes precedence over `default_source`. If neither are set, invoices will use the customer's [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) or [default_source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-default_source).
* `default_source` - (Optional) ID of the default payment source for the subscription. It must belong to the customer associated with the subscription and be in a chargeable state. If `default_payment_method` is also set, `default_payment_method` will take precedence. If neither are set, invoices will use the customer's [invoice_settings.default_payment_method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-invoice_settings-default_payment_method) or [default_source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-default_source).
* `default_tax_rates` - (Optional) The tax rates that will apply to any subscription item that does not have `tax_rates` set. Invoices created will have their `default_tax_rates` populated from the subscription.
* `description` - (Optional) The subscription's description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store an explanation of the subscription for rendering in Stripe surfaces and certain local payment methods UIs.
* `invoice_settings` - (Optional) All invoices will be billed using the specified settings. See [`invoice_settings`](#invoice_settings) below.
* `items` - (Optional) A list of up to 20 subscription items, each with an attached price. See [`items`](#items) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `off_session` - (Optional) Indicates if a customer is on or off-session while an invoice payment is attempted. Defaults to `false` (on-session).
* `on_behalf_of` - (Optional) The account on behalf of which to charge, for each of the subscription's invoices.
* `pause_collection` - (Optional) If specified, payment collection for this subscription will be paused. Note that the subscription status will be unchanged and will not be updated to `paused`. Learn more about [pausing collection](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pause-payment). See [`pause_collection`](#pause_collection) below.
* `payment_behavior` - (Optional) Controls how Stripe handles the first invoice when payment is required and `collection_method=charge_automatically`. Subscriptions with `collection_method=send_invoice` are automatically activated regardless of the first Invoice status. Possible values: `allow_incomplete`, `default_incomplete`, `error_if_incomplete`, `pending_if_incomplete`.
* `payment_settings` - (Optional) Payment settings to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings`](#payment_settings) below.
* `pending_invoice_item_interval` - (Optional) Specifies an interval for how often to bill for any pending invoice items. It is analogous to calling [Create an invoice](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/create) for the given subscription at the specified interval. See [`pending_invoice_item_interval`](#pending_invoice_item_interval) below.
* `proration_behavior` - (Optional) Determines how to handle [prorations](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/prorations) resulting from the `billing_cycle_anchor`. If no value is passed, the default is `create_prorations`. Possible values: `always_invoice`, `create_prorations`, `none`.
* `proration_date` - (Optional) If set, prorations will be calculated as though the subscription was updated at the given time. This can be used to apply exactly the same prorations that were previewed with the [create preview](https://stripe.com/docs/api/invoices/create_preview) endpoint. `proration_date` can also be used to implement custom proration logic, such as prorating by day instead of by second, by providing the time that you wish to use for proration calculations.
* `transfer_data` - (Optional) If specified, the funds from the subscription's invoices will be transferred to the destination and the ID of the resulting transfers will be found on the resulting charges. See [`transfer_data`](#transfer_data) below.
* `trial_end` - (Optional) Unix timestamp representing the end of the trial period the customer will get before being charged for the first time. If set, trial_end will override the default trial period of the plan the customer is being subscribed to. The special value `now` can be provided to end the customer's trial immediately. Can be at most two years from `billing_cycle_anchor`. See [Using trial periods on subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials/free-trials) to learn more.
* `trial_from_plan` - (Optional) Indicates if a plan's `trial_period_days` should be applied to the subscription. Setting `trial_end` per subscription is preferred, and this defaults to `false`. Setting this flag to `true` together with `trial_end` is not allowed. See [Using trial periods on subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials/free-trials) to learn more.
* `trial_period_days` - (Optional) Integer representing the number of trial period days before the customer is charged for the first time. This will always overwrite any trials that might apply via a subscribed plan. See [Using trial periods on subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials/free-trials) to learn more. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `trial_settings` - (Optional) Settings related to subscription trials. See [`trial_settings`](#trial_settings) below.

<a id="automatic_tax"></a>
### `automatic_tax`

The `automatic_tax` attribute supports:

* `disabled_reason` - (Read-Only) If Stripe disabled automatic tax, this enum describes why. Possible values: `requires_location_inputs`.
* `enabled` - (Required) Whether Stripe automatically computes tax on this subscription.
* `liability` - (Optional) The account that's liable for tax. If set, the business address and tax registrations required to perform the tax calculation are loaded from this account. The tax transaction is returned in the report of the connected account. See [`automatic_tax.liability`](#automatic_tax.liability) below.

<a id="automatic_tax.liability"></a>
### `automatic_tax.liability`

The `automatic_tax.liability` attribute supports:

* `account` - (Optional) The connected account being referenced when `type` is `account`.
* `type` - (Required) Type of the account referenced. Possible values: `account`, `self`.

<a id="billing_cycle_anchor_config"></a>
### `billing_cycle_anchor_config`

The `billing_cycle_anchor_config` attribute supports:

* `day_of_month` - (Required) The day of the month of the billing_cycle_anchor.
* `hour` - (Optional) The hour of the day of the billing_cycle_anchor.
* `minute` - (Optional) The minute of the hour of the billing_cycle_anchor.
* `month` - (Optional) The month to start full cycle billing periods.
* `second` - (Optional) The second of the minute of the billing_cycle_anchor.

<a id="billing_mode"></a>
### `billing_mode`

The `billing_mode` attribute supports:

* `flexible` - (Optional) Configure behavior for flexible billing mode See [`billing_mode.flexible`](#billing_mode.flexible) below.
* `type` - (Required) Controls how prorations and invoices for subscriptions are calculated and orchestrated. Possible values: `classic`, `flexible`.
* `updated_at` - (Read-Only) Details on when the current billing_mode was adopted.

<a id="billing_mode.flexible"></a>
### `billing_mode.flexible`

The `billing_mode.flexible` attribute supports:

* `proration_discounts` - (Optional) Controls how invoices and invoice items display proration amounts and discount amounts. Possible values: `included`, `itemized`.

<a id="billing_schedules"></a>
### `billing_schedules`

The `billing_schedules` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `applies_to` - (Optional) Specifies which subscription items the billing schedule applies to. See [`billing_schedules.applies_to`](#billing_schedules.applies_to) below.
* `bill_until` - (Required) Specifies the end of billing period. See [`billing_schedules.bill_until`](#billing_schedules.bill_until) below.
* `key` - (Optional) Unique identifier for the billing schedule.

<a id="billing_schedules.applies_to"></a>
### `billing_schedules.applies_to`

The `billing_schedules.applies_to` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `price` - (Optional) The billing schedule will apply to the subscription item with the given price ID.
* `type` - (Required) Controls which subscription items the billing schedule applies to. Possible values: `price`.

<a id="billing_schedules.bill_until"></a>
### `billing_schedules.bill_until`

The `billing_schedules.bill_until` attribute supports:

* `computed_timestamp` - (Read-Only) The timestamp the billing schedule will apply until.
* `duration` - (Optional) Specifies the billing period. See [`billing_schedules.bill_until.duration`](#billing_schedules.bill_until.duration) below.
* `timestamp` - (Optional) If specified, the billing schedule will apply until the specified timestamp.
* `type` - (Required) Describes how the billing schedule will determine the end date. Either `duration` or `timestamp`. Possible values: `duration`, `timestamp`.

<a id="billing_schedules.bill_until.duration"></a>
### `billing_schedules.bill_until.duration`

The `billing_schedules.bill_until.duration` attribute supports:

* `interval` - (Required) Specifies billing duration. Either `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`. Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`.
* `interval_count` - (Optional) The multiplier applied to the interval.

<a id="billing_thresholds"></a>
### `billing_thresholds`

The `billing_thresholds` attribute supports:

* `amount_gte` - (Optional) Monetary threshold that triggers the subscription to create an invoice
* `reset_billing_cycle_anchor` - (Optional) Indicates if the `billing_cycle_anchor` should be reset when a threshold is reached. If true, `billing_cycle_anchor` will be updated to the date/time the threshold was last reached; otherwise, the value will remain unchanged. This value may not be `true` if the subscription contains items with plans that have `aggregate_usage=last_ever`.

<a id="cancellation_details"></a>
### `cancellation_details`

The `cancellation_details` attribute supports:

* `comment` - (Optional) Additional comments about why the user canceled the subscription, if the subscription was canceled explicitly by the user.
* `feedback` - (Optional) The customer submitted reason for why they canceled, if the subscription was canceled explicitly by the user. Possible values: `customer_service`, `low_quality`, `missing_features`, `other`, `switched_service`, `too_complex`, `too_expensive`, `unused`.
* `feedback_option` - (Optional) Customized feedback options that provide deeper insight into why the subscription was canceled, if the subscription was canceled explicitly by the user.
* `reason` - (Read-Only) Why this subscription was canceled. Possible values: `canceled_by_retention_policy`, `cancellation_requested`, `payment_disputed`, `payment_failed`.

<a id="invoice_settings"></a>
### `invoice_settings`

The `invoice_settings` attribute supports:

* `account_tax_ids` - (Optional) The account tax IDs associated with the subscription. Will be set on invoices generated by the subscription.
* `custom_fields` - (Optional) A list of up to 4 custom fields to be displayed on the invoice. See [`invoice_settings.custom_fields`](#invoice_settings.custom_fields) below.
* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `footer` - (Optional) Footer to be displayed on the invoice.
* `issuer` - (Optional) See [`invoice_settings.issuer`](#invoice_settings.issuer) below.

<a id="invoice_settings.custom_fields"></a>
### `invoice_settings.custom_fields`

The `invoice_settings.custom_fields` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `name` - (Required) The name of the custom field.
* `value` - (Required) The value of the custom field.

<a id="invoice_settings.issuer"></a>
### `invoice_settings.issuer`

The `invoice_settings.issuer` attribute supports:

* `account` - (Optional) The connected account being referenced when `type` is `account`.
* `type` - (Required) Type of the account referenced. Possible values: `account`, `self`.

<a id="items"></a>
### `items`

The `items` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `billed_until` - (Read-Only) The time period the subscription item has been billed for.
* `billing_thresholds` - (Optional) Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the related subscription advanced to a new billing period See [`items.billing_thresholds`](#items.billing_thresholds) below.
* `clear_usage` - (Optional)
* `created` - (Read-Only) Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `current_period_end` - (Read-Only) The end time of this subscription item's current billing period.
* `current_period_start` - (Read-Only) The start time of this subscription item's current billing period.
* `current_trial` - (Optional) The current trial that is applied to this subscription item. See [`items.current_trial`](#items.current_trial) below.
* `deleted` - (Optional)
* `id` - (Optional) Unique identifier for the object.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - (Read-Only) String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `subscription_item`.
* `price` - (Optional) Prices define the unit cost, currency, and (optional) billing cycle for both recurring and one-time purchases of products. [Products](https://docs.stripe.com/api#products) help you track inventory or provisioning, and prices help you track payment terms. Different physical goods or levels of service should be represented by products, and pricing options should be represented by prices. This approach lets you change prices without having to change your provisioning scheme. For example, you might have a single "gold" product that has prices for $10/month, $100/year, and €9 once. Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription), [create an invoice](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/create), and more about [products and prices](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/overview).
* `price_data` - (Optional) See [`items.price_data`](#items.price_data) below.
* `quantity` - (Optional) The [quantity](https://docs.stripe.com/subscriptions/quantities) of the plan to which the customer should be subscribed.
* `subscription` - (Read-Only) The `subscription` this `subscription_item` belongs to.
* `tax_rates` - (Optional) The tax rates which apply to this `subscription_item`. When set, the `default_tax_rates` on the subscription do not apply to this `subscription_item`.

* `product` - (Required)
* `recurring` - (Required) See [`items.price_data.recurring`](#items.price_data.recurring) below.
* `tax_behavior` - (Optional) Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.
* `unit_amount` - (Optional)
* `unit_amount_decimal` - (Optional)

### `items.price_data.recurring`

* `interval_count` - (Optional)

<a id="pause_collection"></a>
### `pause_collection`

The `pause_collection` attribute supports:

* `behavior` - (Optional) The payment collection behavior for this subscription while paused. Possible values: `keep_as_draft`, `mark_uncollectible`, `void`.
* `resumes_at` - (Optional) The time after which the subscription will resume collecting payments.

<a id="payment_settings"></a>
### `payment_settings`

The `payment_settings` attribute supports:

* `payment_method_options` - (Optional) Payment-method-specific configuration to provide to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options) below.
* `payment_method_types` - (Optional) The list of payment method types to provide to every invoice created by the subscription. If not set, Stripe attempts to automatically determine the types to use by looking at the invoice’s default payment method, the subscription’s default payment method, the customer’s default payment method, and your [invoice template settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/invoice).
* `save_default_payment_method` - (Optional) Configure whether Stripe updates `subscription.default_payment_method` when payment succeeds. Defaults to `off`. Possible values: `off`, `on_subscription`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options` attribute supports:

* `acss_debit` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the Canadian pre-authorized debit payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit) below.
* `bancontact` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the Bancontact payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.bancontact`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.bancontact) below.
* `billie` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the Billie payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie) below.
* `blik` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the Blik payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.blik`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.blik) below.
* `card` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the Card payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.card`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.card) below.
* `customer_balance` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the Bank transfer payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.customer_balance`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.customer_balance) below.
* `payto` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the PayTo payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto) below.
* `pix` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the Pix payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix) below.
* `upi` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the UPI payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi) below.
* `us_bank_account` - (Optional) This sub-hash contains details about the ACH direct debit payment method options to pass to invoices created by the subscription. See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account) below.

### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options`

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.bancontact"></a>

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.billie"></a>

* `line2` - (Optional) Address line 2 (for example, apartment, suite, unit, or building).

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.card"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.card`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.card` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.card.mandate_options`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.card.mandate_options) below.
* `network` - (Optional) Selected network to process this Subscription on. Depends on the available networks of the card attached to the Subscription. Can be only set confirm-time. Possible values: `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `girocard`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `unknown`, `visa`.
* `request_three_d_secure` - (Optional) We strongly recommend that you rely on our SCA Engine to automatically prompt your customers for authentication based on risk level and [other requirements](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). However, if you wish to request 3D Secure based on logic from your own fraud engine, provide this option. Read our guide on [manually requesting 3D Secure](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/3d-secure/authentication-flow#manual-three-ds) for more information on how this configuration interacts with Radar and our SCA Engine. Possible values: `any`, `automatic`, `challenge`.

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.card.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) Amount to be charged for future payments, specified in the presentment currency.
* `amount_type` - (Optional) One of `fixed` or `maximum`. If `fixed`, the `amount` param refers to the exact amount to be charged in future payments. If `maximum`, the amount charged can be up to the value passed for the `amount` param. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `description` - (Optional) A description of the mandate or subscription that is meant to be displayed to the customer.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.customer_balance"></a>

* `funding_type` - (Optional) The funding method type to be used when there are not enough funds in the customer balance. Permitted values include: `bank_transfer`. Possible values: `bank_transfer`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.customer_balance.bank_transfer"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.customer_balance.bank_transfer`

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.customer_balance.bank_transfer.eu_bank_transfer"></a>

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options) below.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) The maximum amount that can be collected in a single invoice. If you don't specify a maximum, then there is no limit.
* `amount_type` - (Read-Only) Only `maximum` is supported. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `purpose` - (Optional) The purpose for which payments are made. Has a default value based on your merchant category code. Possible values: `dependant_support`, `government`, `loan`, `mortgage`, `other`, `pension`, `personal`, `retail`, `salary`, `tax`, `utility`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix` attribute supports:

* `expires_after_seconds` - (Optional) The number of seconds (between 10 and 1209600) after which Pix payment will expire. Defaults to 86400 seconds.
* `mandate_options` - (Optional) See [`payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options`](#payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options) below.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) Amount to be charged for future payments.
* `amount_includes_iof` - (Optional) Determines if the amount includes the IOF tax. Possible values: `always`, `never`.
* `end_date` - (Optional) Date when the mandate expires and no further payments will be charged, in `YYYY-MM-DD`.
* `payment_schedule` - (Optional) Schedule at which the future payments will be charged. Possible values: `halfyearly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `weekly`, `yearly`.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi` attribute supports:

### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) Amount to be charged for future payments.
* `amount_type` - (Optional) One of `fixed` or `maximum`. If `fixed`, the `amount` param refers to the exact amount to be charged in future payments. If `maximum`, the amount charged can be up to the value passed for the `amount` param. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `description` - (Optional) A description of the mandate or subscription that is meant to be displayed to the customer.

<a id="payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections"></a>
### `payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections`

The `payment_settings.payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections` attribute supports:

<a id="pending_invoice_item_interval"></a>
### `pending_invoice_item_interval`

The `pending_invoice_item_interval` attribute supports:

* `interval` - (Required) Specifies invoicing frequency. Either `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`. Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`.
* `interval_count` - (Optional) The number of intervals between invoices. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months. Maximum of one year interval allowed (1 year, 12 months, or 52 weeks).

<a id="transfer_data"></a>
### `transfer_data`

The `transfer_data` attribute supports:

* `amount_percent` - (Optional) A non-negative decimal between 0 and 100, with at most two decimal places. This represents the percentage of the subscription invoice total that will be transferred to the destination account. By default, the entire amount is transferred to the destination.
* `destination` - (Required) The account where funds from the payment will be transferred to upon payment success.

<a id="trial_settings"></a>
### `trial_settings`

The `trial_settings` attribute supports:

* `end_behavior` - (Required) Defines how a subscription behaves when a trial ends. See [`trial_settings.end_behavior`](#trial_settings.end_behavior) below.

<a id="trial_settings.end_behavior"></a>
### `trial_settings.end_behavior`

The `trial_settings.end_behavior` attribute supports:

* `billing_cycle_anchor` - (Optional) Indicates how the subscription's billing cycle anchor is reset when a trial ends. If not set, the default is `now`. Possible values: `now`, `unchanged`.
* `missing_payment_method` - (Optional) Indicates how the subscription should change when the trial ends if the user did not provide a payment method. Possible values: `cancel`, `create_invoice`, `pause`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `application` - ID of the Connect Application that created the subscription.
* `canceled_at` - If the subscription has been canceled, the date of that cancellation. If the subscription was canceled with `cancel_at_period_end`, `canceled_at` will reflect the time of the most recent update request, not the end of the subscription period when the subscription is automatically moved to a canceled state.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `ended_at` - If the subscription has ended, the date the subscription ended.
* `latest_invoice` - The most recent invoice this subscription has generated over its lifecycle (for example, when it cycles or is updated).
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `managed_payments` - Settings for Managed Payments for this Subscription and resulting [Invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/object) and [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object). See [`managed_payments`](#managed_payments) below.
* `next_pending_invoice_item_invoice` - Specifies the approximate timestamp on which any pending invoice items will be billed according to the schedule provided at `pending_invoice_item_interval`.
* `pending_setup_intent` - You can use this [SetupIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents) to collect user authentication when creating a subscription without immediate payment or updating a subscription's payment method, allowing you to optimize for off-session payments. Learn more in the [SCA Migration Guide](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/migration/strong-customer-authentication#scenario-2).
* `pending_update` - If specified, [pending updates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pending-updates) that will be applied to the subscription once the `latest_invoice` has been paid. See [`pending_update`](#pending_update) below.
* `presentment_details` - See [`presentment_details`](#presentment_details) below.
* `schedule` - The schedule attached to the subscription
* `start_date` - Date when the subscription was first created. The date might differ from the `created` date due to backdating.
* `status` - Possible values are `incomplete`, `incomplete_expired`, `trialing`, `active`, `past_due`, `canceled`, `unpaid`, or `paused`. For `collection_method=charge_automatically` a subscription moves into `incomplete` if the initial payment attempt fails. A subscription in this status can only have metadata and default_source updated. Once the first invoice is paid, the subscription moves into an `active` status. If the first invoice is not paid within 23 hours, the subscription transitions to `incomplete_expired`. This is a terminal status, the open invoice will be voided and no further invoices will be generated. A subscription that is currently in a trial period is `trialing` and moves to `active` when the trial period is over. A subscription can only enter a `paused` status [when a trial ends without a payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials/free-trials#create-free-trials-without-payment). A `paused` subscription doesn't generate invoices and can be resumed after your customer adds their payment method. The `paused` status is different from [pausing collection](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pause-payment), which still generates invoices and leaves the subscription's status unchanged. If subscription `collection_method=charge_automatically`, it becomes `past_due` when payment is required but cannot be paid (due to failed payment or awaiting additional user actions). Once Stripe has exhausted all payment retry attempts, the subscription will become `canceled` or `unpaid` (depending on your subscriptions settings). If subscription `collection_method=send_invoice` it becomes `past_due` when its invoice is not paid by the due date, and `canceled` or `unpaid` if it is still not paid by an additional deadline after that. Note that when a subscription has a status of `unpaid`, no subsequent invoices will be attempted (invoices will be created, but then immediately automatically closed). After receiving updated payment information from a customer, you may choose to reopen and pay their closed invoices. Possible values: `active`, `canceled`, `incomplete`, `incomplete_expired`, `past_due`, `paused`, `trialing`, `unpaid`.
* `status_details` - Describes changes to the subscription's status. See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.
* `test_clock` - ID of the test clock this subscription belongs to.
* `trial_start` - If the subscription has a trial, the beginning of that trial.

<a id="managed_payments"></a>
### `managed_payments`

The `managed_payments` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Set to `true` to enable [Managed Payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments), Stripe's merchant of record solution, for this session.

<a id="pending_update"></a>
### `pending_update`

The `pending_update` attribute supports:

* `billing_cycle_anchor` - If the update is applied, determines the date of the first full invoice, and, for plans with `month` or `year` intervals, the day of the month for subsequent invoices. The timestamp is in UTC format.
* `cancel_at_period_end` - Indicates whether this subscription should cancel at the end of the current period if the update is applied.
* `discount` - The pending subscription-level discount that will be applied when the pending update is applied. See [`pending_update.discount`](#pending_update.discount) below.
* `discounts` - The discounts that will be applied to the subscription when the pending update is applied. Use `expand[]=discounts` to expand each discount.
* `expires_at` - The point after which the changes reflected by this update will be discarded and no longer applied.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `subscription_items` - List of subscription items, each with an attached plan, that will be set if the update is applied. See [`pending_update.subscription_items`](#pending_update.subscription_items) below.
* `trial_end` - Unix timestamp representing the end of the trial period the customer will get before being charged for the first time, if the update is applied.
* `trial_from_plan` - Indicates if a plan's `trial_period_days` should be applied to the subscription. Setting `trial_end` per subscription is preferred, and this defaults to `false`. Setting this flag to `true` together with `trial_end` is not allowed. See [Using trial periods on subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials/free-trials) to learn more.

<a id="pending_update.discount"></a>
### `pending_update.discount`

The `pending_update.discount` attribute supports:

* `checkout_session` - The Checkout session that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular session in payment mode. Not present for subscription mode.
* `customer` - The ID of the customer associated with this discount.
* `customer_account` - The ID of the account representing the customer associated with this discount.
* `end` - If the coupon has a duration of `repeating`, the date that this discount will end. If the coupon has a duration of `once` or `forever`, this attribute will be null.
* `id` - The ID of the discount object. Discounts can't be fetched by ID. Use `expand[]=discounts` in API calls to expand discount IDs in an array.
* `invoice` - The invoice that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice.
* `invoice_item` - The invoice item `id` (or invoice line item `id` for invoice line items of type='subscription') that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice item or invoice line item.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `discount`.
* `promotion_code` - The promotion code applied to create this discount.
* `source` - See [`pending_update.discount.source`](#pending_update.discount.source) below.
* `start` - Date that the coupon was applied.
* `subscription` - The subscription that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription.
* `subscription_item` - The subscription item that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription item.

<a id="pending_update.discount.source"></a>
### `pending_update.discount.source`

The `pending_update.discount.source` attribute supports:

* `coupon` - The coupon that was redeemed to create this discount.
* `type` - The source type of the discount. Possible values: `coupon`.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items`

The `pending_update.subscription_items` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `billed_until` - The time period the subscription item has been billed for.
* `billing_thresholds` - Define thresholds at which an invoice will be sent, and the related subscription advanced to a new billing period See [`pending_update.subscription_items.billing_thresholds`](#pending_update.subscription_items.billing_thresholds) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `current_period_end` - The end time of this subscription item's current billing period.
* `current_period_start` - The start time of this subscription item's current billing period.
* `current_trial` - The current trial that is applied to this subscription item. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.current_trial`](#pending_update.subscription_items.current_trial) below.
* `discounts` - The discounts applied to the subscription item. Subscription item discounts are applied before subscription discounts. Use `expand[]=discounts` to expand each discount.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `subscription_item`.
* `price` - Prices define the unit cost, currency, and (optional) billing cycle for both recurring and one-time purchases of products. [Products](https://docs.stripe.com/api#products) help you track inventory or provisioning, and prices help you track payment terms. Different physical goods or levels of service should be represented by products, and pricing options should be represented by prices. This approach lets you change prices without having to change your provisioning scheme. For example, you might have a single "gold" product that has prices for $10/month, $100/year, and €9 once. Related guides: [Set up a subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/set-up-subscription), [create an invoice](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/invoices/create), and more about [products and prices](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/overview). See [`pending_update.subscription_items.price`](#pending_update.subscription_items.price) below.
* `quantity` - The [quantity](https://docs.stripe.com/subscriptions/quantities) of the plan to which the customer should be subscribed.
* `subscription` - The `subscription` this `subscription_item` belongs to.
* `tax_rates` - The tax rates which apply to this `subscription_item`. When set, the `default_tax_rates` on the subscription do not apply to this `subscription_item`. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates`](#pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates) below.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.billing_thresholds"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.billing_thresholds`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.billing_thresholds` attribute supports:

* `usage_gte` - Usage threshold that triggers the subscription to create an invoice

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.current_trial"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.current_trial`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.current_trial` attribute supports:

* `end_date` -
* `start_date` -
* `trial_offer` -

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.price"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.price`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.price` attribute supports:

* `active` - Whether the price can be used for new purchases.
* `billing_scheme` - Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `unit_amount` or `unit_amount_decimal`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for prices with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for prices with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes. Possible values: `per_unit`, `tiered`.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `currency_options` - Prices defined in each available currency option. Each key must be a three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) and a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). See [`pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options`](#pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options) below.
* `custom_unit_amount` - When set, provides configuration for the amount to be adjusted by the customer during Checkout Sessions and Payment Links. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.price.custom_unit_amount`](#pending_update.subscription_items.price.custom_unit_amount) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `lookup_key` - A lookup key used to retrieve prices dynamically from a static string. This may be up to 200 characters.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `nickname` - A brief description of the price, hidden from customers.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `price`.
* `product` - The ID of the product this price is associated with.
* `recurring` - The recurring components of a price such as `interval` and `usage_type`. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.price.recurring`](#pending_update.subscription_items.price.recurring) below.
* `tax_behavior` - Only required if a [default tax behavior](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/products-prices-tax-categories-tax-behavior#setting-a-default-tax-behavior-(recommended)) was not provided in the Stripe Tax settings. Specifies whether the price is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unspecified`. Once specified as either `inclusive` or `exclusive`, it cannot be changed. Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.
* `tiers` - Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.price.tiers`](#pending_update.subscription_items.price.tiers) below.
* `tiers_mode` - Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price. In `graduated` tiering, pricing can change as the quantity grows. Possible values: `graduated`, `volume`.
* `transform_quantity` - Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the amount billed. Cannot be combined with `tiers`. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.price.transform_quantity`](#pending_update.subscription_items.price.transform_quantity) below.
* `type` - One of `one_time` or `recurring` depending on whether the price is for a one-time purchase or a recurring (subscription) purchase. Possible values: `one_time`, `recurring`.
* `unit_amount` - The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options` attribute is a map. Each value supports:

* `custom_unit_amount` - When set, provides configuration for the amount to be adjusted by the customer during Checkout Sessions and Payment Links. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount`](#pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount) below.
* `tax_behavior` - Only required if a [default tax behavior](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/products-prices-tax-categories-tax-behavior#setting-a-default-tax-behavior-(recommended)) was not provided in the Stripe Tax settings. Specifies whether the price is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unspecified`. Once specified as either `inclusive` or `exclusive`, it cannot be changed. Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.
* `tiers` - Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.tiers`](#pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.tiers) below.
* `unit_amount` - The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - The unit amount in cents (or local equivalent) to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if `billing_scheme=per_unit`.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.custom_unit_amount` attribute supports:

* `maximum` - The maximum unit amount the customer can specify for this item.
* `minimum` - The minimum unit amount the customer can specify for this item. Must be at least the minimum charge amount.
* `preset` - The starting unit amount which can be updated by the customer.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.tiers"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.tiers`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.price.currency_options.tiers` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `flat_amount` - Price for the entire tier.
* `flat_amount_decimal` - Same as `flat_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.
* `unit_amount` - Per unit price for units relevant to the tier.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - Same as `unit_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.
* `up_to` - Up to and including to this quantity will be contained in the tier.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.price.custom_unit_amount"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.price.custom_unit_amount`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.price.custom_unit_amount` attribute supports:

* `maximum` - The maximum unit amount the customer can specify for this item.
* `minimum` - The minimum unit amount the customer can specify for this item. Must be at least the minimum charge amount.
* `preset` - The starting unit amount which can be updated by the customer.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.price.recurring"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.price.recurring`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.price.recurring` attribute supports:

* `interval` - The frequency at which a subscription is billed. One of `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`. Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`.
* `interval_count` - The number of intervals (specified in the `interval` attribute) between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months.
* `meter` - The meter tracking the usage of a metered price
* `usage_type` - Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either `metered` or `licensed`. `licensed` automatically bills the `quantity` set when adding it to a subscription. `metered` aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to `licensed`. Possible values: `licensed`, `metered`.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.price.tiers"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.price.tiers`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.price.tiers` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `flat_amount` - Price for the entire tier.
* `flat_amount_decimal` - Same as `flat_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.
* `unit_amount` - Per unit price for units relevant to the tier.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - Same as `unit_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places.
* `up_to` - Up to and including to this quantity will be contained in the tier.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.price.transform_quantity"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.price.transform_quantity`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.price.transform_quantity` attribute supports:

* `divide_by` - Divide usage by this number.
* `round` - After division, either round the result `up` or `down`. Possible values: `down`, `up`.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `active` - Defaults to `true`. When set to `false`, this tax rate cannot be used with new applications or Checkout Sessions, but will still work for subscriptions and invoices that already have it set.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the tax rate for your internal use only. It will not be visible to your customers.
* `display_name` - The display name of the tax rates as it will appear to your customer on their receipt email, PDF, and the hosted invoice page.
* `effective_percentage` - Actual/effective tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true, this percentage reflects the rate actually used to calculate tax based on the product's taxability and whether the user is registered to collect taxes in the corresponding jurisdiction.
* `flat_amount` - The amount of the tax rate when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. Tax rates with `rate_type` `percentage` can vary based on the transaction, resulting in this field being `null`. This field exposes the amount and currency of the flat tax rate. See [`pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates.flat_amount`](#pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates.flat_amount) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `inclusive` - This specifies if the tax rate is inclusive or exclusive.
* `jurisdiction` - The jurisdiction for the tax rate. You can use this label field for tax reporting purposes. It also appears on your customer’s invoice.
* `jurisdiction_level` - The level of the jurisdiction that imposes this tax rate. Will be `null` for manually defined tax rates. Possible values: `city`, `country`, `county`, `district`, `multiple`, `state`.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `tax_rate`.
* `percentage` - Tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true, this percentage includes the statutory tax rate of non-taxable jurisdictions.
* `rate_type` - Indicates the type of tax rate applied to the taxable amount. This value can be `null` when no tax applies to the location. This field is only present for TaxRates created by Stripe Tax. Possible values: `flat_amount`, `percentage`.
* `state` - [ISO 3166-2 subdivision code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2), without country prefix. For example, "NY" for New York, United States.
* `tax_type` - The high-level tax type, such as `vat` or `sales_tax`. Possible values: `amusement_tax`, `communications_tax`, `digital_excise_tax`, `gst`, `hst`, `igst`, `jct`, `lease_tax`, `mass_transit_parking_tax`, `parking_tax`, `pst`, `qst`, `retail_delivery_fee`, `rst`, `sales_tax`, `service_tax`, `utility_users_tax`, `vat`.

<a id="pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates.flat_amount"></a>
### `pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates.flat_amount`

The `pending_update.subscription_items.tax_rates.flat_amount` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount of the tax when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. This positive integer represents how much to charge in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).
* `currency` - Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase.

<a id="presentment_details"></a>
### `presentment_details`

The `presentment_details` attribute supports:

* `presentment_currency` - Currency used for customer payments.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `paused` - Indicates when and why the subscription transitioned to the paused status. See [`status_details.paused`](#status_details.paused) below.

<a id="status_details.paused"></a>
### `status_details.paused`

The `status_details.paused` attribute supports:

* `subscription` - Information on the `type=subscription` pause. See [`status_details.paused.subscription`](#status_details.paused.subscription) below.
* `transitioned_at` - Unix timestamp in seconds of when the subscription status transitioned to `paused`.
* `type` - The type of pause. Possible values: `subscription`.

<a id="status_details.paused.subscription"></a>
### `status_details.paused.subscription`

The `status_details.paused.subscription` attribute supports:

* `type` - The reason that the subscription was paused. Possible values: `final_payment_failure`, `first_payment_failure`, `pause_requested`, `system`, `trial_end_without_payment_method`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a subscription using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_subscription.team
  id = "sub_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_subscription.team
  identity = {
    id = "sub_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the subscription.

Using `terraform import`, import a subscription using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_subscription.team sub_123
```

~> Importing a subscription adopts every item it has, so a configuration that lists fewer items deletes the rest on the next apply.
